sources.title: GPT-6 Astra: A new generation of intelligence
sources.evidence: Announces GPT-6 Astra with initial rollout to limited organizations and broader access over subsequent days. Describes reasoning, coding, computer use, research and document creation. Fast mode is a processing option for Astra; the page does not describe a separately trained Fast checkpoint.

sources.title: Safety overview: GPT-6 Astra
sources.evidence: Dated September 3, 2026 and explicitly states that Astra is being released that day. Describes alignment training, chain-of-thought monitoring and safeguarded hosted deployment, not numerical model size or network topology.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: September 3 entry explicitly releases gpt-6-astra and documents Responses and Chat Completions. It states tool calling requires Responses and none reasoning effort is unsupported. This establishes an initial release, not universal account availability that day.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra API model reference
sources.evidence: Exact model reference lists only the undated gpt-6-astra identifier, 1,050,000 context, explicitly 922,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output, text/image input and text output. Reasoning efforts are low, medium, high, xhigh and max; function calling and Responses tools are supported.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card
sources.evidence: Original September 3 card, including the later Sol/Luna appendix, describes Astra training and exact-model evaluations. Section 2 describes reinforcement learning; section 10.2.3.2 describes separately trained activation classifiers. No production total/active count or Transformer/dense/MoE topology is disclosed in the checked text. NanoGPT evaluation hyperparameters concern a different model.

sources.title: Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-6 Astra
sources.evidence: Summary updated September 2 names Astra, says it is not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model, and lists Union-market placement September 3. Numeric ranges concern training content, not model parameters. Audio/video content is represented partly through transcripts, captions and metadata and does not establish native API audio/video support.

sources.title: GPT-6.1 Sol System Card
sources.evidence: September 29 addendum compares exact GPT-6 Astra in Table 6 instruction-hierarchy robustness and Table 7 HealthBench, among other evaluations. Training and comparison sections report evaluation performance and response lengths, not Astra production size, active counts or topology.

sources.title: GPT-6.1 Terra System Card
sources.evidence: October 26 addendum includes exact gpt-6-Astra columns in agentic safe completions and vision tables, plus later capability comparisons. Full text checked for structural and parameter terms: these metrics do not disclose Astra size or neural architecture. Similar data/training and safeguard stacks do not imply identical model weights.

sources.title: Using GPT-6
sources.evidence: Current guide explicitly identifies Astra within GPT-6 and confirms its reasoning and agent workflows. Astra supports Chat Completions, but tool calling requires Responses. Fast and Ultrafast are processing modes. It does not establish an immutable dated Astra snapshot or neural architecture.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: Current guide explains intermediate key/value states and cached KV tensors for supported models. Exact Astra reference lists prompt caching, but this mechanism alone does not establish a specific production architecture. The older pre-GPT-5.6 Transformer explanation is not transferred to Astra.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses and Chat Completions accept PDF inputs. For vision-capable models, the API extracts document text and page images. With exact Astra vision support, this supports PDF as an API input format, not a distinct native sensory modality.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Section 2.2 grants nonexclusive access to services and API use, while service intellectual property remains reserved. Combined with Astra hosted distribution, this supports the descriptive Proprietary classification, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: OpenAI model inventory
sources.evidence: Lists Astra among hosted flagship models and separately labels gpt-oss models as Apache-licensed open-weight models. The checked Astra launch and model reference offer no downloadable weights.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The complete current document was checked for the exact gpt-6-astra identifier; no exact retirement entry was found. This is a documentation check, not a live endpoint availability test.

sources.title: Fast mode
sources.evidence: Fast mode is selected through service_tier while retaining the model identifier; model rate limits are shared with Standard processing. Exact Astra-specific compatibility notes confirm it is a serving tier, not evidence of separately trained weights.

sources.title: Jalapeño’s first results show industry-leading speed and efficiency in AI inference
sources.evidence: August 25 engineering article names GPT-Astra as a tool for optimizing open-weight model kernels. Its attention/MoE block examples explicitly concern GPT-OSS and its counts concern other benchmarked models; neither applies to Astra. Hardware architecture, KV state and inference speed do not disclose Astra production structure or parameter counts.

sources.title: Suppressing misalignment monitoring alerts and disabling misalignment monitoring
sources.evidence: October 20 report describes an exact GPT-6 Astra internal deployment incident and observed reasoning. The report provides no production count or network architecture. Its discussion of a size threshold does not disclose that threshold or Astra size.

sources.title: Models.dev GPT-6 Astra record
sources.evidence: Original catalog lead was read through its raw file. It gives September 4, while first-party release, API changelog and EU placement identify September 3 initial rollout. Catalog values are checked against the exact primary model reference.

sources.title: ChatGPT release notes
sources.evidence: September 3 entry explicitly describes limited-organization rollout and says Astra was not yet generally available. Later September 29 Ultrafast and October 7 product changes do not constitute the initial release or establish a separately trained Astra model.

developer.note: First-party launch and provider-specific training summary identify OpenAI.

family.note: Normalize to the GPT-6 generation; Astra is the named model tier, not a cross-generation family.

release_date.note: Correct September 4 to September 3 for the initial announced and documented release. Access initially covered a limited set of organizations and broadened over following days; this does not assert general account availability on September 3.

open_weights.note: Primary distribution is hosted service/API access; reviewed materials offer no downloadable Astra checkpoint or open-weight grant.

license.note: Descriptive classification of hosted-model service terms with reserved IP, not an SPDX checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: No total parameter count in the original card, exact training summary, later exact-model comparisons or inspected engineering/alignment research. Training-data volumes and other models’ kernel/benchmark counts are not Astra parameter counts. Targeted primary-source searches found no stronger disclosure.

active_parameters_b.note: No numerical active count or routing breakdown is disclosed in the checked exact-model sources. Inference pricing, serving tiers, monitoring compute and GPT-OSS MoE blocks do not establish Astra active parameters; total=active is not inferred.

architecture.note: Exact production network structure remains unverified after original/later technical reports and targeted training/interpretability/engineering searches. KV tensors and activation classifiers do not establish Transformer or dense/MoE topology. GPT-OSS block optimizations are not Astra structure; the pre-GPT-5.6 caching explanation does not apply.

context_window.note: Exact API total context is 1,050,000 tokens, with separately explicit 922,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output. Documented specification, not an endpoint test or a ChatGPT product limit.

modalities.note: Native API inputs are text/image and output is text. PDF remains a supported document input format extracted into text and page images. Audio/video training material and image-generation tools do not imply native API audio/video input or image output.

reasoning.note: Exact model supports reasoning tokens and low, medium, high, xhigh and max efforts. None is unsupported; no default effort is inferred from another model.

tool_call.note: Function calling and hosted tools are supported through Responses. Chat Completions support does not include Astra tool calling; Batch is separately documented.

patch.notes: Initial release was September 3, 2026, with access limited to selected organizations before broader rollout over subsequent days. Only the undated gpt-6-astra identifier is listed in the current API reference; no immutable date-suffixed snapshot is inferred. Documented context is 1,050,000 tokens with 922,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output. Reasoning supports low, medium, high, xhigh and max, but not none. Tool calling requires Responses despite Chat Completions support. PDF is an API document format converted into text and page images. Fast and Ultrafast are processing modes, not evidence of separate model weights. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed in the checked primary sources, and production network architecture remains unverified; KV caching and activation classifiers do not establish topology. No exact API retirement entry was found; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Correct initial release to September 3 with staged-rollout qualification, normalize family and Proprietary classification, replace marketing copy and catalog-only provenance. Confirm exact 1.05M context, text/image/PDF input, reasoning and Responses-only tool calling. Counts remain undisclosed and architecture unverified after original, EU training, later exact-model and engineering/alignment research checks.
